officialTitle: Adjuvant Pertuzumab and Trastuzumab in Early HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: After surgery and central HER2-positive confirmation, 4,805 patients with node-positive or high-risk node-negative BC were randomly assigned (1:1) to either 1-year pertuzumab or placebo added to standard adjuvant chemotherapy and 1-year trastuzumab.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding pertuzumab to adjuvant trastuzumab and chemotherapy improve invasive disease-free survival in operable HER2-positive breast cancer?

pico.population: Node-positive or high-risk node-negative operable HER2-positive breast cancer
pico.intervention: Pertuzumab for 1 year plus trastuzumab and standard adjuvant chemotherapy
pico.comparator: Placebo plus trastuzumab and standard adjuvant chemotherapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: IDFS. Secondary: OS, cardiac and general safety

arms.label: Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Pertuzumab, trastuzumab and standard adjuvant chemotherapy

arms.label: Placebo + trastuzumab + chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Placebo, trastuzumab and standard adjuvant chemotherapy

publications.label: 6-year follow-up (second interim OS analysis)

outcomes.sourceQuote: Disease recurrence occurred in 171 patients (7.1%) in the pertuzumab group and 210 patients (8.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.00; P=0.045). The estimates of the 3-year rates of invasive-disease-free survival were 94.1% in the pertuzumab group and 93.2% in the placebo group.

In the cohort of patients with node-positive disease, the 3-year rate of invasive-disease-free survival was 92.0% in the pertuzumab group, as compared with 90.2% in the placebo group (hazard ratio for an invasive-disease event, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.96; P=0.02).

In the cohort of patients with node-negative disease, the 3-year rate of invasive-disease-free survival was 97.5% in the pertuzumab group and 98.4% in the placebo group (hazard ratio for an invasive-disease event, 1.13; 95% CI, 0.68 to 1.86; P=0.64).
IDFS analysis based on 508 events (intent-to-treat population) showed a hazard ratio of 0.76 (95% CI, 0.64 to 0.91) and 6-year IDFS of 91% and 88% for pertuzumab and placebo groups, respectively.
The node-positive cohort continues to derive clear IDFS benefit from pertuzumab (hazard ratio 0.72 [95% CI, 0.59 to 0.87]), 6-year IDFS being 88% and 83%, respectively.

This interim OS analysis comparing pertuzumab versus placebo did not reach the= .0012 level required for statistical significance (= .17, hazard ratio 0.85). Six-year OS were 95% versus 94% with 125 deaths (5.2%) versus 147 (6.1%), respectively.

safety.sourceQuote: Diarrhea of grade 3 or higher occurred almost exclusively during chemotherapy and was more frequent with pertuzumab than with placebo (9.8% vs. 3.7%).
Primary cardiac events remain < 1% in both the treatment groups.

strengths: Long-term follow-up with prespecified OS analyses
limitations: Small absolute IDFS benefit in the overall population
No benefit seen in the node-negative cohort
OS not statistically significant at the reported interim analysis

clinicalImplications.text: Supports adding pertuzumab to adjuvant trastuzumab and chemotherapy for higher-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer, particularly node-positive disease, where the IDFS benefit is concentrated.

tumourBoardPearl.text: The benefit of adjuvant pertuzumab is driven by node-positive disease; in node-negative patients no IDFS benefit was seen.
